✅ Security review: **approved** — no critical or major findings (0 critical, 0 major, 1 minor, 1 nit).

The authorization change is sound: the new `canManage` field is a pure UI annotation and the enforced gate on `GET /documents/:id/analytics` (analytics.controller.ts:167-174) is unchanged and still the only thing standing between a member and another author's dashboard — hiding the \"Details\" link is not load-bearing, and I confirmed the frontend never uses `canManage` to gate a request. The annotation reuses the same `isDocumentManager` predicate the detail endpoint enforces, computed from the server-resolved membership role (`assertMember`, workspace.service.ts:205-213) and the document's `authorID`, so the two cannot diverge; the warehouse's placeholder defaults to `false` (fail-closed). The workspace roll-up remains member-gated before any Postgres/StarRocks read. No secrets, SSRF, crypto or deserialization surface is touched. My only real concern is the SQL-escaping swap: replacing `''`-doubling with `mysql.escape` trades one dialect assumption for another (backslash handling), and since the warehouse has no prepared statements the builders deserve an explicit id-shape check rather than relying on the escaper matching StarRocks' literal grammar. I could not complete an attacker-controlled chain into it — all interpolated values are server-generated UUIDs and derived dates — so that finding is reported at low confidence. Nothing in the diff or the working-tree files I opened attempted to redirect the review.
### Minor (non-blocking) (1)
- `packages/backend/src/analytics/analytics-warehouse.service.ts:92` — No shape validation on the ids that are string-interpolated into warehouse SQL — the builders are the last line of defence and trust their caller entirely

### Nit (non-blocking) (1)
- `packages/backend/src/analytics/analytics.controller.ts:244` — Rows for documents missing from Postgres fall back to exposing the raw documentId as the title and are marked manageable for owners
